'''HireRight''' is a global family of background screening companies based in [[Nashville, Tennessee]], United States, and [[Delaware General Corporation Law|registered in Delaware]]. In 2012, its HireRight Solutions Inc. entity was the first employment background screening firm the [[Federal Trade Commission]] (FTC) ever charged with violating the [[Fair Credit Reporting Act]] (FCRA).<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 10, 2012 |title=FTC Fines Employee Background Screening Company $2.6 Million for Alleged FCRA Violations |url=https://www.hunton.com/privacy-and-cybersecurity-law-blog/ftc-fines-employee-background-screening-company-2-6-million-for-alleged-fcra-violations |access-date=June 17, 2026 |website=Hunton Andrews Kurth LLP}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

Although the company became public via an [[initial public offering]] in 2021 with a listing on the [[New York Stock Exchange]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Linnane |first=Caira |date=October 29, 2021 |title=HireRight IPO prices at $19 a share, below proposed price range of $21 to $24 |url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/hireright-ipo-prices-at-19-a-share-below-proposed-price-range-of-21-to-24-2021-10-29 |website=MarketWatch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/general-atlantic-backed-hireright-files-us-ipo-2021-10-06/ |title=General Atlantic-backed HireRight files for U.S. IPO |date=October 6, 2021 |publisher=Reuters}}</ref> in 2024, [[private equity]] firms [[General Atlantic]] and Stone Point Capital acquired the company for $1.65&nbsp;billion.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/stone-point-general-atlantic-buy-hireright-165-bln-deal-2024-02-16/ |title=Stone Point, General Atlantic raise offer to buy HireRight to $1.65 bln deal |date=February 16, 2024 |publisher=Reuters}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dorbian |first=Iris |date=February 16, 2024 |title=General Atlantic and Stone Point to take background screening firm HireRight private |url=https://www.pehub.com/general-atlantic-and-stone-point-to-take-background-screening-firm-hireright-private/ |website=PE Hub}}</ref> The transaction closed on June 28, 2024.<ref>[https://ir.hireright.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/242/hireright-announces-completion-of-acquisition-by-general HireRight Announces Completion of Acquisition by General Atlantic and Stone Point Capital]</ref>

== Acquisitions and mergers ==

=== Powerchex ===

On June 23, 2010, HireRight announced that it had acquired Powerchex, a UK-based [[pre-employment screening]] company specialising in the financial services sector in the [[City of London]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Third of applicants tell lies to get a job|publisher= ERT Weekly|date= September 1, 2005|url= http://www.accessmylibrary.com/premium/0286/0286-11432072.html}}</ref> Powerchex was a full member of the UK chapter of the National Association of Professional Background Screeners or NAPBS,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20220802104442/http://www.powerchex.co.uk/documents/NAPBS%20press%20release.pdf Powerchex Joins the National Association of professional background Screeners] </ref> and was started by [[Alexandra Kelly]] in 2005 who is the former [[Director (business)|managing director]] and owner of the company.

In October 2010, Powerchex was rebranded as HireRight.<ref name="hireright.com">{{cite web |title=Kroll Background Worldwide And Powerchex Unite Under HireRight Brand |url=https://www.hireright.com/news/press-release/kroll-background-worldwide-and-powerchex-unite-under-hireright-brand |website=HireRight |accessdate=11 October 2019}}</ref>

Both Powerchex and Kroll Background Screening (below) are now fully owned subsidiaries of HireRight.

=== Kroll ===
On August 3, 2010, HireRight then-parent company [[Altegrity Risk International]] announced it had completed the acquisition of [[Kroll Inc.]] from [[Marsh & McLennan Companies]] in an all-cash transaction valued at US$1.13 billion. In October 2010, Kroll Background Worldwide was rebranded as HireRight.<ref name="hireright.com"/>

On March 13, 2018, it was reported that [[Duff & Phelps]] Corp. would buy Kroll, Inc. (which did not include background screening portion of the former Kroll business that had been rebranded with HireRight brands).<ref name=wsj-banerji>{{cite news |last=Banerji |first=Gunjan |date=March 13, 2018 |title=Duff & Phelps to Buy Corporate-Investigations Firm Kroll |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/duff-phelps-to-buy-corporate-investigations-firm-kroll-1520973140?mod=WSJ_Markets_LEFTTopStories&tesla=y | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |location=The New York Times, New York City, United States |access-date=March 17, 2018}}</ref>  On June 4, 2018, the transaction was completed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Duff & Phelps Announces New Business Unit After Completing Kroll Acquisition |url=https://www.duffandphelps.com/about-us/news/duff-and-phelps-announces-new-business-unit-after-completing-kroll-acquisition}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Kroll's History |url=https://www.kroll.com/en/about-us/history |website=Kroll |accessdate=11 October 2019}}</ref>

=== General Information Services ===

On Friday, May 25, 2018, HireRight and General Information Services (GIS) announced their intent and agreement to a merger.<ref>{{cite web | title=HireRight and GIS to Merge |url=https://www.hireright.com/news/press-release/hireright-and-gis-to-merge |website=HireRight |accessdate=11 October 2019}}</ref> The companies announced the closing of the merger on July 12, 2018.<ref>{{cite web | title=HireRight and GIS Ownership Complete Merger|url=https://www.hireright.com/news/press-release/hireright-and-gis-ownership-complete-merger |website=HireRight |accessdate=11 October 2019}}</ref> The resulting combined group is the largest provider of background screening services in the United States. Following the merger, HireRight rebranded, with both HireRight and GIS using the new branding.<ref>{{cite web | title=New HireRight, New Look|url=https://www.hireright.com/news/press-release/new-hireright-new-look |website=HireRight |accessdate=11 October 2019}}</ref>

=== J-Screen and PeopleCheck ===
On October 12, 2019, HireRight announced the acquisition of J-Screen in Japan and PeopleCheck in Australia.<ref>{{cite web | title=HireRight Strengthens Global Offering with Two Key Acquisitions in Japan and Australia|url=https://www.hireright.com/news/press-release/hireRight-strengthens-global-offering-with-japan-and-australia |website=HireRight |accessdate=11 October 2019}}</ref>

== Legal issues with service ==

HireRight was the subject of a number of class-action and [[Fair Credit Reporting Act|FCRA]] lawsuits.<ref name="wsj-screening" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Litigation: Wirt v. Altegrity, Inc. & HireRight, Inc. |url=https://lac.org/what-we-do/criminal-justice/litigation-wirt-v-altegrity-inc-hireright-inc/ |website=Legal Action Center |accessdate=11 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190511205610/https://www.lac.org/what-we-do/criminal-justice/litigation-wirt-v-altegrity-inc-hireright-inc/|archive-date=2019-05-11}}</ref> In 2011 the company paid $28 million to plaintiffs who accused HireRight of failing to provide copies of reports to job applicants and failing to resolve disputes.<ref name="wsj-screening">{{cite web |last1=Chao |first1=Loretta |title=Driver-Screening Firms Draw Scrutiny |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/driver-screening-firms-draw-scrutiny-1476869402 |website=Wall Street Journal |accessdate=10 May 2019 |date=19 October 2016}}</ref> And on August 8, 2012, the US Department of Justice announced HireRight settled charges of violating the FCRA for $2.6M.<ref name="wsj-screening" /><ref name=":0">{{cite web |author1=Office of Public Affairs |title=Employment Screening Services Provider Settles Charges of Violating Fair Credit Reporting Act |url=https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/2012/August/12-civ-986.html |website=www.justice.gov |publisher=Department of Justice |language=en |date=8 August 2012|accessdate=11 May 2019}}</ref>

Companies that use background check services must follow FCRA procedures or face class-action liability with millions of dollars in exposure.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Holland |first1=Ron |last2=Batten |first2=Jonathan |title=FCRA 101: How to Avoid Risky Background Checks |url=https://www.shrm.org/resourcesandtools/hr-topics/talent-acquisition/pages/fcra-avoid-risky-background-checks.aspx |website=SHRM |accessdate=11 May 2019 |date=20 October 2017}}</ref> According to a Wall Street Journal investigation into hiring practices in the trucking industry, class-action lawsuits were brought against trucking companies over how they use HireRight.<ref name="wsj-screening" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Job applicants claim inaccurate background check report prevent them from finding a job {{!}} New York Consumer Law Blog |url=https://nyconsumerlaw.com/lawyer/2017/05/18/Background-Check-Errors/Job-applicants-claim-inaccurate-background-check-report-prevent-them-from-finding-a-job_bl29952.htm |website=Law Office of Adam G. Singer |accessdate=11 May 2019}}</ref> HireRight customer U.S. Xpress settled in 2013 for $2.75M, and Swift in 2014 for $4.4M over their failure to disclose hiring practices.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kell-Holland |first1=Clarissa |title=U.S. Xpress settles for $2.75 million in lawsuit over background checks |url=http://www.landlinemag.com/story.aspx?storyid=61995 |website=Land Line Magazine |accessdate=11 May 2019 |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190511010417/http://www.landlinemag.com/story.aspx?storyid=61995#.XNYflBOmN24|archive-date=2019-05-11}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Barradas |first1=Samuel |title=Illegal Background Checks Cost U.S. Xpress $2.75 Million |url=https://www.thetruckersreport.com/illegal-background-checks-cost-u-s-xpress-2-75-million/ |website=TruckersReport.com |accessdate=11 May 2019 |date=11 April 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Jaillet |first1=James |title=Swift makes $4.4 million settlement with 160,000 driver applicants over background checks |url=https://www.overdriveonline.com/swift-makes-4-4-million-settlement-with-160000-driver-applicants-over-background-checks/ |website=Overdrive |date=23 April 2014 |accessdate=27 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Arnall Golden Gregory LLP-Montserrat C. |title=Swift Transportation Company, background checks and the FCRA {{!}} Lexology |url=https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=1146c316-4e54-4d3d-9748-3983fc933723 |website=Lexology |date=5 May 2014 |accessdate=11 May 2019 |language=en}}</ref>
